paper_title: MARBLE A Hard Benchmark for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning and Planning
caption: : Search space of the dataset under different configurations.

annotations.annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of missing pieces and the number of possible solutions in the search space of M-Cube. The x-axis represents the number of missing pieces, labeled "# Missing pieces," with a linear scale ranging from 1 to 6, and tick labels appear at each integer value. The y-axis represents the number of possible solutions, labeled "# Possible solutions," with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^2 to 10^8, with tick labels at 10^2, 10^4, 10^6, and 10^8. There are two lines in the plot. The first line, which represents "Flip needed," is colored yellow with circular markers and a solid line style. It begins just above (1, 10) and ends just above (6, 10^8), showing an upward trend across the x-axis. The second line, representing "Flip ignored," is colored blue with circular markers and a solid line style. It starts around just above (1, 10) and ends just below (6, 10^7), also displaying an upward trend. Notable points labeled on the plot include "CUBE-easy" just below (2, 100) and "CUBE" around (6, 10^8). A legend is placed at the top left corner of the plot.
